key_insight: A small number of high‑norm "outlier" tokens appear in both the encoder and denoiser of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs), disproportionately attracting attention while carrying little local information; detecting and taming these outliers improves generation stability and image quality.
problem_solved: Outlier tokens in RAE‑DiT pipelines create attention imbalance and hinder generative performance and robustness; prior work noted outliers in ViTs but did not address their role or mitigation in diffusion‑based generative models.
method: Empirical diagnosis: analyze token‑norm distributions and attention attribution in pretrained ViT encoders and DiT denoisers to locate outlier tokens.

Targeted mitigation: introduce lightweight detection + suppression strategies (e.g., token‑norm clipping / adaptive reweighting / normalization or token dropout) applied to encoder and denoiser to reduce outlier influence.
Evaluation: measure effects on generation quality and training/inference stability in RAE‑DiT pipelines, comparing attention patterns and visual outputs before vs. after intervention.
impact: Provides a practical, low‑cost way to make transformer‑based diffusion models more stable and higher quality by addressing a previously underexplored failure mode; easy to integrate into existing DiT and ViT workflows for improved reliability in image generation.
visual_elements: Histogram or violin plot of token‑norm distribution highlighting a few high‑norm outliers
Side‑by‑side attention maps (before vs. after taming) showing attention concentration vs. more balanced attention
Pipeline diagram (RAE encoder → DiT denoiser) with an inset showing outlier detection + suppression module
Before/after image pairs (generated samples) and a compact metric bar chart (e.g., FID/consistency) to illustrate quality/stability gains
paper_title: Taming Outlier Tokens in Diffusion Transformers
paper_authors: Xiaoyu Wu, Yifei Wang, Tsu-Jui Fu, Liang-Chieh Chen, Zhe Gan
